shard_zero_overhead.method: Sum successful step durations whose unchanged validate.yml condition is exactly matrix.shard == 0; common provisioning and PR-only steps are excluded. Job and step timestamps come from the same attempt-1 REST jobs responses as the module baseline.

selection: Latest successful main push on each of 2026-10-13, 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15 before 05:50Z; attempt 1 only, all eight shards successful.

method.name: native-durations-with-completion-delta-overhead
method.description: For each primary verbose unittest event before Slowest test durations, use its terminal-outcome timestamp (on the header or last terminal line before the next header). Subtract the preceding completion timestamp; initialize it with the first header timestamp. Use the larger of that nonnegative delta and the native --durations 50 value when present, retaining fixture/log-delivery overhead. Map case IDs through each run's report.json inventory to native discovery owners, sum by owner, then take the median across observed runs. Missing modules are absent observations, not zeros.
method.evidence_class: Derived scheduling proxy from real CI; native per-test samples and job/step durations are measured, module totals include fixture/log delivery effects.
method.upstream: python/cpython@v3.12.3 Lib/unittest/runner.py:_printDurations; Lib/unittest/case.py:TestCase.run; GitHub Actions REST workflow-jobs docs, accessed 2026-10-15
limitations: Historical successful runs are different repository revisions; this is scheduling evidence, not a paired performance experiment.
Only the 50 slowest native test durations per shard are emitted. Remaining durations and overhead are timestamp proxies; the first event can omit a duration unless included in the native table.
Each reconstructed shard suite is within 0.37 seconds of the native suite total; this checks gross accounting, not isolated per-module precision.
Job times include provisioning and other steps; the scheduling bound covers module execution only and excludes queues and shard-0-only validators.
Unknown future modules retain the planner's 10-second fallback; refresh this table when CI provides new evidence.
